title: Weak Nouns
subtitle: Guma, sunne, ēage — the -an declension.
objectives: Understand and apply the concepts of Weak Nouns.
Read and parse examples from authentic Old English texts.

sections.heading: Core concept
sections.body: Weak nouns are simpler than strong nouns. Most forms end in -an. Three genders, but the pattern is similar across all three. The weak declension includes many common nouns (guma 'man', nama 'name', sunne 'sun', ēage 'eye', ēare 'ear').

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: Guma (man): se guma (nom), þone guman (acc), þæs guman (gen), þǣm guman (dat).

items.prompt: What is the main concept of this lesson?

items.answer: Review the paradigm and example above.
